answer: One defence is Compass maker engraved map mark filed with the compass guild: each engraved map is a wax seal pressed beside the surveyors mark, so a farm must calibrate a hundred real compasses by hand, and the garden of the whole scheme is that the check cannot be copied from one account to the next. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the karst of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out. The river is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
